terms.grammar: neuter of the interrogative pronoun quis
evidence: Cic. Att. 7.11.1: quaesō, quid est hoc?
terms.comment: With a genitive it asks how much of a thing: quid novī?, what news?; quid cēnae?, what is there for dinner? (Ter. Haut. 211). Quid? alone also asks why: see “why”.

evidence: Publ. Q 80: Quod quisque amat, laudandō commendat sibi.
terms.comment: The “what” of a statement, “I like what you made”: id quod, or quod alone when its clause comes first.

phrases.latin: Quid fēcī? quid commeruī aut peccāvī, pater?
phrases.english: What have I done? What have I deserved, Father, or what wrong have I done?

phrases.latin: Quid ais? quid nōmen tibi est?
quaesō, quid est hoc? aut quid agitur? mihi enim tenebrae sunt
phrases.english: tell me, what is this? What is going on? I am in the dark
so what did you have at dinner?

phrases.latin: Quod quisque amat, laudandō commendat sibi.
phrases.english: What each of us loves, we make dearer to ourselves by praising it.
